digest.en: U.S. Treasury Secretary's comments on a potential Hormuz deal with Iran by August 5 lead the board, as US missile arsenals dwindle. Meanwhile, Ukraine's drone strikes in Russia and Colombia's anti-corruption activist senator inauguration also grab attention.
digest.hi: भारतीय क्रू समेत 14 लोगों को बचाने के बाद, यमन तट के पास डूबे जहाज की जांच जारी है। इस घटना ने अमेरिका-ईरान तनाव के बीच एक और मोड़ ला दिया है, जिसमें भारतीय नागरिक भी शामिल हैं।

articles.title: U.S. Treasury Secretary says chance of Hormuz deal with Iran by August 5
articles.summary: "We are in talks with the Iranians, and I think there is a chance we may have a deal today or tomorrow to open the strait and move towards a more normalised position in this conflict," says Scott Bessent U. S. Treasury Secretary says chance of Hormuz deal with Iran by August 5.

articles.title: US in a losing race to replenish depleted missile arsenals
articles.summary: The US’s multibillion-dollar push to expand interceptor missile production could begin rebuilding depleted stocks, but long manufacturing lead times, industrial bottlenecks and cost imbalances mean the benefits will depend on how quickly new capacity translates into deployable missiles. The US Department of Defense (DoD) signed framework agreements worth over US$3 billion with defense contractors US in a losing race to replenish depleted missile arsenals.

articles.title: Ukrainian Drones Strike 'Russia's Amazon' Near St. Petersburg
articles.summary: Russian authorities claim Ukrainian drones hit multiple Wildberries warehouses in several regions on August 4. Officials reported damage at facilities near St. Petersburg, and in the Tver and Moscow regions. Ukraine's drone commander said at least 15 Wildberries hubs have been hit since mid-July. Ukrainian Drones Strike 'Russia's Amazon' Near St. Petersburg.

articles.title: Russian Drone Hunts Down Market Vendor in Kherson
articles.summary: Ukrainian National Police have published a video they say shows a Russian drone stalking and attacking a man selling goods at a market in the city of Kherson. The 52-year-old survived but suffered blast trauma, concussion, and shrapnel wounds, according to authorities. Russian Drone Hunts Down Market Vendor in Kherson.

articles.title: Ukrainian Strikes On Russian Warehouses, Including Wildberries, Leaves 5 Dead
articles.summary: Ukrainian drones struck two more warehouses used by the online retailer Wildberries, as well as a third in the Moscow region that killed five people as Russia and Ukraine continued exchanging cross-border strikes with US-mediated peace talks stalled. Ukrainian Strikes On Russian Warehouses, Including Wildberries, Leaves 5 Dead.

articles.title: Colombia swears in costumed anti-corruption activist as senator
articles.summary: Luis Carlos Rúa revealed himself to be Elefante blanco just three days before election for ‘his own safety’. Now he is tackling graft from senate floorWhen 102 senators were sworn in for Colombia’s latest parliamentary session, they included 32 women, 69 men – and one cartoon elephant. Colombia swears in costumed anti-corruption activist as senator.

articles.title: Japan’s prime minister tours earthquake-hit sites as recovery efforts hampered by soaring
articles.summary: Prime minister Sanae Takaichi visited Kumamoto prefecture almost a week after a magnitude 7.1 quake hit, killing 38 peopleJapan’s prime minister, Sanae Takaichi, has visited the south-western prefecture of Kumamoto, where recovery efforts are being hampered by heat and a lack of water supplies, almost a week after a magnitude 7.1 earthquake killed dozens and caused widespread damage. Thirty-eight p Japan’s prime minister tours quake-hit sites as recovery efforts hampered by soaring temperatures.

articles.title: Stronger EU borders needed after Ceuta crisis, von der Leyen says
articles.summary: European Commission president says work needed in five areas of migration control including returning more peopleThe president of the European Commission has called for action to strengthen Europe’s borders after tens of thousands of people arrived and quickly left the Spanish territory of Ceuta, triggering a furious row between Madrid and other European countries. Stronger EU borders needed after Ceuta crisis, von der Leyen says.

articles.title: How Ceuta migrant crisis exposes divisions within Europe
articles.summary: Dozens of people died attempting to reach the Spanish enclave of Ceuta after an estimated 50,000 crossed from Morocco last week. The incident has led to a political crisis in Spain and criticism from EU countries. Lucy Hough speaks to the Guardian’s European community affairs correspondent, Ashifa Kassam – watch on YouTube Continue reading How Ceuta migrant crisis exposes divisions within Europe.

articles.title: Beyond the Singularity: China owning the physical AI revolution
articles.summary: The global discourse on artificial intelligence is preoccupied with a dramatic possibility: The Singularity, the moment a disembodied artificial general intelligence awakens in a server farm, escapes human control and either elevates or destroys civilization. This is largely a software-centered vision of the future, shaped by a culture that tends to imagine intelligence as something [] The post B Beyond the Singularity: China owning the physical AI revolution.

articles.title: How India’s ‘Cockroach’ movement grew its wings
articles.summary: Young people across India recently made international headlines for mass protests over the recurring leaks of entrance exams that help students qualify for medical schools and highly coveted government jobs. The Gen Z protesters won a major victory within a matter of weeks when Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on July 25, 2026, bowing to [] The post How India’s ‘Cockroach’ movement.

articles.title: New centre opens at heart of record Ebola outbreak
articles.summary: New UN-backed centres will serve eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) as confirmed Ebola cases continued to climb sharply over the weekend in the largest ever outbreak of the highly contagious disease in the country. New centre opens at heart of record Ebola outbreak. New UN-partnered centres will serve eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) as confirmed Ebola cases continued to climb sharply over the weekend in the largest-ever outbreak of the highly contagious disease in the country.

articles.title: Ukraine Hits Another Wildberries Hub, This Time In Russia's Vladimir Region
articles.summary: Ukraine has launched another drone strike targeting a Wildberries warehouse overnight on August 3, according to Russian authorities. The attack in the Vladimir region is part of a broader campaign in recent weeks that has repeatedly hit the logistics network of Russia's largest online retailer. Ukraine Hits Another Wildberries Hub, This Time In Russia's Vladimir Region.

articles.title: Russian Logistics Sites Targeted Again As Zelenskyy Urges Faster Patriot Deliveries
articles.summary: Ukraine and Russia exchanged another wave of overnight drone strikes targeting logistics, energy, and civilian infrastructure, as President Volodymyr Zelenskyy voiced frustration with Western allies over delays in delivering urgently needed Patriot air defense systems and other military aid. Russian Logistics Sites Targeted Again As Zelenskyy Urges Faster Patriot Deliveries.

articles.title: Yen hits three-month high after Trump helps prop up currency
articles.summary: US and Japanese governments confirm they carried out a rare joint intervention late last weekWhy has Trump stepped in to prop up Japan’s currency? Business live – latest updatesThe yen has hit its highest level in three months after Japan and the US launched a combined operation to support the Japanese currency. Yen hits three-month high after Trump helps prop up currency.

articles.title: Austria breaks heat records as Japan braces for Typhoon Dolphin
articles.summary: Soaring temperatures continue to sweep parts of Europe, while Okinawa faces powerful winds and storm surgesEurope live – latest updatesUnbearable, record-breaking heat has dominated the summer of 2026 across much of Europe. articles.title: Chaos of border crossing gives way to limbo for Moroccans on Ceuta’s streets
articles.summary: People among the more than 50,000 who entered Spanish enclave this week describe the journey and their prospectsFour days ago, Youssef El Abbas saw an opportunity to reclaim the life he had lost seven years earlier. News was circulating that about 400 people had swum from Morocco to the neighbouring Spanish enclave of Ceuta on the north African coast, approximately 12 miles (19km) across the strai.

articles.title: Trapped by a Facebook job advert, freed by a stranger in a taxi
articles.summary: Sofia* was 27, raising her seven-year-old son alone in Venezuela, and running out of options. For years she had distributed personal hygiene products door to door, but as her customers’ finances collapsed, so did her income. Trapped by a Facebook job advert, freed by a stranger in a taxi.

articles.title: At Least 3 Killed, 21 Wounded In Moscow Restaurant Bombing, Russian Authorities Say
articles.summary: Russian authorities said on August 2 that an improvised explosive device was detonated at a restaurant in central Moscow, killing three people and wounding 21 others, as investigators worked to determine who was behind the bombing. 3 Killed, 21 Wounded In Moscow Restaurant Bombing, Russian Authorities Say.

articles.title: For These Ukrainian Soldiers, Accepting Death Proved The Key To Living
articles.summary: When Serhiy Kutrakov decided to take up arms in 2014 to defend Ukraine from Russian-backed separatists, he accepted he would likely be killed in combat. Documentarian Yulia Hontaruk followed Kutrakov and two other soldiers on and off the battlefield for 12 years. For These Ukrainian Soldiers, Accepting Death Proved The Key To Living.

articles.title: Trump Says He Called Off Impending Attack On Iran, Insists Deal Is Close
articles.summary: Trump said he has decided to hold off on new attacks on Iran, claiming the perimeters of a deal have been agreed with Tehran and that Israel is joining the US President Donald Trump said he has decided to "hold off" on any new attacks on Iran, saying "the perimeters" of a deal have been agreed to with Tehran and adding that Israel was joining him in the commitment.

articles.title: Anti-LGBTQ+ laws are on the rise across west Africa, campaigners warn
articles.summary: Activists in the region say politicians regard LGBTQ+ people as ‘the easiest scapegoats to maintain their power’A growing number of west African countries are implementing or strengthening anti-LGBTQ+ laws, amid local political pressures and a global pushback against LGBTQ+ rights. In March, Senegal doubled the maximum prison sentence for gay sex to 10 years and criminalised the “promotion” of homo Anti-LGBTQ+ laws are on the rise across west Africa, campaigners warn.

articles.title: Tourist plane crashes during flight over Peru’s Nazca Lines, killing 13
articles.summary: Aircraft crashes into field after departing from the nearby city of Ica, according to local authoritiesAt least 13 people have died after a plane carrying tourists crashed into a field in Peru, local authorities said. Aircraft crashes into field after departing from the nearby city of Pisco, according to local authorities At least 13 people, among them foreign tourists, have been killed in a plane crash in southern Peru, near the Nazca Lines, police reported on Saturday. Local authorities in Nazca confirmed that 11 tourists and two pilots died when the Cessna Grand Caravan crashed in Pueblo Viejo, approximately.

articles.title: Zelenskyy Says 'Answers' Needed On Patriot Delivery As Civilian Death Toll Climbs
articles.summary: In the wake of the latest deadly Russian air strikes on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy expressed frustration with his Western allies, urging speedier delivery of urgently needed Patriot air defense missiles and other weapons. Zelenskyy Says 'Answers' Needed On Patriot Delivery As Civilian Death Toll Climbs.

articles.title: Strong El Niño ahead, UN weather agency warns
articles.summary: As much of the world faces grapples with above normal temperatures and major rainfall changes, the UN Meteorological Organization (WMO) warned on Friday that El Niño, a powerful climate pattern shaping global weather, will intensify starting next month. Strong El Niño ahead, UN weather agency warns.

articles.title: ‘गोलियां चलाकर जनता का कर रहे दमन’, भारत ने PoJK चुनाव पर पाक को दिखाया आईना
articles.summary: पाकिस्तान के कब्जे वाले कश्मीर में वोटिंग बायकॉट और तनाव के बीच भारत ने पाक को आईना दिखाया। पाकिस्तान के कब्जे वाले कश्मीर (PoK) में वोटिंग बायकॉट और जारी तनाव की स्थिति के बीच मंगलवार (4 अगस्त, 2026) को दो विधानसभा सीटों पर मतदान हो रहा है. इन दोनों विधानसभा सीटों पर मतदान रविवार (2 अगस्त, 2026) को तय किया गया था, लेकिन मुजफ्फराबाद-1 और मुजफ्फराबाद-2 के सभी मतदान केंद्रों पर सड़क बंद, विरोध प्रदर्शन और आगजनी की घटनाएं होने की वजह से वोटिंग नहीं हो पाई थी.

articles.title: क्या सुप्रीम कोर्ट के फैसले से शादीशुदा और लिव-इन पार्टनर में कोई फर्क नहीं?
articles.summary: सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने 3 अगस्त 2026 को फैसला सुनाया कि लिव-इन पार्टनर भी क्रूरता से सुरक्षा पा सकते हैं. जस्टिस संजय करोल और जस्टिस विक्रम नाथ की पीठ ने कहा कि अगर कोई पुरुष किसी महिला के साथ 'शादी जैसे रिश्ते' में रह रहा है, तो उस पर IPC की धारा 498A के तहत मुकदमा चलाया जा सकता है. यह फैसला लिव-इन रिलेशनशिप को कानूनी तौर पर नई पहचान देता है.

articles.title: CJP के अभिजीत दीपके और सौरव दास की बढ़ी मुश्किलें, बंगाल में दर्ज हुई FIR
articles.summary: पश्चिम बंगाल में सिलीगुड़ी साइबर क्राइम पुलिस स्टेशन में अभिजीत दीपके, सौरव दास और सीजेपी आयोजकों के खिलाफ पॉक्सो अधिनियम की धारा 13, 14 और 15 और बीएनएस की धारा 153 के तहत एफआईआर दर्ज की गई है. इससे पहले दिल्ली पुलिस से शिकायत की गई थी कि दीपके ने एक इन्फ्लुएंसर को धमकी दी थी. कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी (CJP) संस्थापक अभिजीत दीपके की मुश्किलें बढ़ती हुई नजर आ रही हैं.
